findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: tagDeviceUI sets the device's local cache entry before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and leaves that entry in place when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Although this change propagates the error for the first request, a second request with the same device ID hits the cache and returns nil, so Anonymous.Authenticate grants access. A rejected device can therefore bypass the configured limit simply by retrying, for the 29-minute cache lifetime. Cache only successful admissions (and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful).

findings.title: Requests without a device header bypass limit enforcement
findings.body: Authentication now relies on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached to enforce the limit, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. An anonymous client can omit that client-controlled header and still receive an authenticated anonymous identity even when the device limit is full, without being counted. The limited authentication path needs to handle missing device IDs explicitly rather than treating an untracked request as an admitted device.

findings.title: Device admission count and insertion are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and subsequently inserts in another, without locking or an atomic admission mechanism. When the count is one below the limit, concurrent requests for distinct device IDs can all observe available capacity and all insert successfully. This allows the active device count to exceed the configured limit, including across Grafana instances sharing the database. Serialize the capacity check and admission using a database-coordinated mechanism and add a concurrent admission test.
